title: A customer about slot 11's rushed work: a control arm changed and nobody checked the alignment
purpose: People, slot 11, the first of the two complaints. The clunk is gone and the steering wheel sits crooked: the last check was skipped. The customer quotes what the mechanic said to him at pick-up. Travis does not defend it, books the recheck for the same day at no charge and sums it up. An existing-job call: no score.

scenario.who_calls: Phil Cantrell, who had his car in three days earlier.
scenario.job: front lower control arm, driver's side, replaced on the Tuesday; no alignment was done or checked
scenario.wants: the steering wheel straight, without paying for an alignment he should have had
scenario.what_happens: He says the wheel sits crooked and the car drifts, that there is no alignment on his ticket, and what the mechanic told him at pick-up. Travis says it should have been checked, apologises, books the car for two o'clock that day at no charge with the foreman rechecking the arm, and sums up with the address.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Travis.
Travis, Phil Cantrell. I had — I had my Malibu in there Tuesday.
Yes sir, Mr. Cantrell. Lower control arm, driver's side. What's going on?
Well, the clunk's gone, I'll give you that. But ever since I picked it up my steerin' wheel sits crooked. I'm — I'm goin' straight down the road with the wheel cocked over to the right.
Okay. Is it pulling on you, or does it track straight with the wheel off?
It drifts left a little. And I — and I looked at my ticket, and I don't see an alignment on it anywhere.
Uh... no sir, there's not one on here. There should've been. You can't swap a control arm and not at least check it.
That's what my brother-in-law said. I asked — I asked the fella about it when I picked it up — Dustin, it says on here — and he told me it was fixed and he didn't know what else to tell me.
Yeah.
He said that to you?
Word for word.

Okay. Well, I know what else to tell you. That's on us, and I'm — I'm sorry you had to call. Bring it back and we'll put it on the alignment rack, no charge, and I'll have Randy, our shop foreman, go back over that arm himself.
Okay.
I don't wanna pay for an alignment I shoulda got the first time.
You're not paying for anything. It's like getting a new door hung and nobody checked that it shuts — that's part of the job. Can you get it here today at two?
I can do two.
Okay. It's about an hour. You can wait, or I'll run you back to work.
I'll wait on it.
Alright. So that's today at two, here at twenty-one-oh-six East Main. Randy rechecks the control arm, we align it, and there's no charge for any of it.
Okay.
Alright, Travis. I appreciate you makin' it right.
Yes sir. Ask for me when you get here.
